gucs.name: bioseq.diagnostics.logging.enabled
gucs.purpose: Enable or dissable internal logging. BioseqDB internally supports logging to file, but current builds are all configured to use only postgres logging mechanisms.

value_descriptions.false: Disable internal logger.
value_descriptions.true: Enable internal logger.

gucs.name: bioseq.testing.chunked_scanner.enabled
gucs.purpose: Forces BioseqDB to load entire sequence into memory and create 'fake' lazy-loading interface that accesses it. Used by me to test C++ interface for lazy-loading.

value_descriptions.false: Use the normal scanner.
value_descriptions.true: Force load entire sequence into memory and create lazy-loader interface for that RAM sequence.

gucs.name: bioseq.testing.in_memory_scanner.enabled
gucs.purpose: Forces BioseqDB to load entire sequence into memory and passes it directly to the pipeline. (Note that this is the same for user as bioseq.testing.chunked_scanner.enabled with the only difference being internally used C++ API). Used by me to test C++ interface for lazy-loading.

value_descriptions.false: Use the normal scanner.
value_descriptions.true: Force load entire sequence into memory and pass it directly to the pipeline.

gucs.name: bioseq.testing.persisted_index.failure_mode
gucs.purpose: Cause 'fake' index reader failure to be reported during queries.

value_descriptions.unsupported_vector_shape: Make the index reader report an unsupported vector shape (due to wrong w/k etc. parameters used during index build).

gucs.name: bioseq.storage.compression.algorithm
gucs.conditional_default: zstd if compiled, otherwise lz4 if compiled, otherwise pglz
gucs.purpose: Choose the compression algorithm used for storing data columns

value_descriptions.zstd: Use Zstandard when compiled in. This is the preferred build-time default.
value_descriptions.lz4: Use LZ4 when compiled in. This becomes the default when Zstandard is unavailable.
value_descriptions.pglz: Use Postgres built-in coded. This becomes the default when neither of previous two is available.

gucs.notes: Changing the default does not rewrite any existing indices!

gucs.name: bioseq.storage.compression.level
gucs.purpose: Set the zstd compression level if zstd is used.

gucs.name: bioseq.storage.stripe.row_limit
gucs.purpose: Sets the maximum rows in a new table's column stripe, when writing rows. Existing table options and stored stripes are unchanged.

gucs.name: bioseq.storage.chunk_group.row_limit
gucs.purpose: Sets the maximum rows in a new table's chunk group, when writing rows. Chunk groups divide a stripe into smaller column-reading units.

gucs.name: bioseq.storage.dml.enabled
gucs.purpose: Special setting that controls whether reads apply deleted-row masks.

value_descriptions.true: Default, shouldn't be changed. Normally deleted rows that are marked as such, should not be returned in queries.
value_descriptions.false: Bypass any deletion filtering. Useful for debugging, the queries will return all rows including deleted ones. Note that if the table is rewritten using VACCUM FULL, then deleted rows will physically dissapear!

gucs.name: bioseq.execution.parallel.enabled
gucs.purpose: Enable Postgres parallel queries

value_descriptions.true: Allow possible parallel scan paths (actual worker availability still depends on PostgreSQL planner, so this setting does not force the planner to use parallel scans). Additionally, any query using mmsearch won't be parallelized, due to current code architecture. The parallel scans however are possible for metadata queries.
value_descriptions.false: Disable all parallel scans on BioseqDB tables.

gucs.notes: Alignment won't use parallel scans even with this setting enabled.

gucs.name: bioseq.execution.parallel.minimum_processes
gucs.purpose: Requests the PostgreSQL worker count for possbible Bioseq parallel scan paths. This is soft minimum and the actual worker count is determined by the PostgreSQL planner.

gucs.name: bioseq.vectorization.enabled
gucs.purpose: Can disable vectorized SQL operations for aggregates like SUM(), COUNT(), etc.

value_descriptions.true: Use supported vectorized SQL operations when the plan allows them.
value_descriptions.false: Use normal SQL processing for those operations.

gucs.notes: Vectorized operations only apply to non-sequence aggregates, not alignment pipeline.

gucs.name: bioseq.column_cache.enabled
gucs.purpose: Controls the backend's decompressed column-chunk cache.

value_descriptions.true: After decompression save the buffer, so it's avaialable for reuse
value_descriptions.false: Read and decompress but do not save buffers in cache.

gucs.notes: Decompression cache only applies to one query. After completion of the query, the cache is cleared.

gucs.name: bioseq.column_cache.capacity_mb
gucs.purpose: Limits the decompressed column-chunk cache
gucs.notes: BioseqDB will still allocate buffers for decompression, so this setting does not control the total memory used during decompression

gucs.name: bioseq.planner.index_scan.enabled
gucs.purpose: Can allow usage of non-BioseqDB indices with BioseqDB tables.

value_descriptions.true: Allow using non-BioseqDB indices during queries, for example it becomes possible to use B-tree index on metadata column.
value_descriptions.false: Do not allow using any non-BioseqDB indices on BioseqDB tables. This can heavily degrade performance as Postgres will select plan that ignores existing B-trees, hash indexes etc.

gucs.notes: This settings does not control any BioseqDB indices like MPF/MPS etc.

gucs.name: bioseq.planner.custom_scan.enabled
gucs.purpose: Entirely disable all BioseqDB custom scans.

value_descriptions.true: Allow the planner to install Bioseq custom scans.
value_descriptions.false: Disable custom scans. This means that it won't be possible to use 'mmsearch' function anymore as it requires custom scan path. All other metadata queries still will be possible.

gucs.notes: Useful to force Postgres to select non-BioseqDB plans. Do not use this unless you know what you're doing.

gucs.name: bioseq.planner.custom_scan.max_paths
gucs.purpose: Limit paths explored by GQO for BioseqDB custom scans. Increasing the number may yield better plans, but increase planning time.

gucs.name: bioseq.planner.qual_pushdown.enabled
gucs.purpose: Controls behaviour of predicate pushdown.

value_descriptions.true: Normally filters can be pushed down into the scan, which improved performance. The predicates that Postgres reports as highly-correlated will be used to possibly reduce number of loaded chunks (min/max prunning mechanism)
value_descriptions.false: Leave predicates outside the scan, which may severely degrade performance.

gucs.notes: Pushdown uses correlation statistics for column reported by Postgres to decide if this predicate can be useful to avoid loading chunks

gucs.name: bioseq.planner.qual_pushdown.correlation_threshold
gucs.purpose: Sets the minimum absolute column correlation value (reported by Postgres table statistics) used by chunk prunning logic described for bioseq.planner.qual_pushdown.enabled. Values closer to one, mean stronger correlation.

gucs.name: bioseq.planner.diagnostics.log_level
gucs.purpose: Chooses the PostgreSQL severity for planner diagnostic messages (logging levels are Postgres specific).
gucs.notes: PostgreSQL's message thresholds determine where the messages appear.

gucs.name: bioseq.planner.sequence_sort_scan.enabled
gucs.purpose: Enable or disable custom sort for BioseqDB sequences. Sort works only if there's single sorting key that is sequence column itself.

value_descriptions.false: Use default Postgres sort.
value_descriptions.true: Consider the custom batch-sort where possible.

gucs.name: bioseq.index.insert_maintenance.enabled
gucs.purpose: Enables automatic index incremental update when row is inserted into the table.

value_descriptions.false: Save new source rows without automatic index builds.
value_descriptions.true: Currently grouped MPF index (the default one) does not support this function and reports an error.

gucs.notes: You can always still manually update index via update_index function.

gucs.name: bioseq.index.sequence_read.enabled
gucs.purpose: Controls whether the pipeline executor can read indexes. If the option is disabled, then pipeline will always recompute all seeds from scratch.

value_descriptions.true: Normally allow reading BioseqDB indices.
value_descriptions.false: Force pipeline to always recompute all seeds from scratch.

gucs.notes: There's also per-search option passed via aligner_options: index_read_requirement codes 1 and 2 override this setting.

gucs.name: bioseq.index.async_persistence.enabled
gucs.purpose: Very experimental setting that allows main process to asynchronously update missing indices for sequences: If query does not have seeds in index for certain sequence and needs to compute them, after the query the index will be updated.

value_descriptions.false: Do not stage asynchronous persistence work.
value_descriptions.true: Allow the limited ordinary-MPS submission path when its other requirements are met.

gucs.notes: Grouped MPF index (default) does not implement this feature and using it with this option enabled will produce an error. Additionally you need to enable bioseq.index.recompute_async_persistence.enabled as well.

gucs.name: bioseq.index.recompute_async_persistence.enabled
gucs.purpose: Separate setting, but effectively to enable async persistence you need to enable bioseq.index.async_persistence.enabled together with this one.

value_descriptions.false: Same as bioseq.index.async_persistence.enabled
value_descriptions.true: Same as bioseq.index.async_persistence.enabled

gucs.notes: Set bioseq.index.async_persistence.enabled to the same value as this one.

gucs.name: bioseq.index.memory_cap_mb
gucs.purpose: Specialized limit on the memory allocated by index builders/readers in MB. Using 0 means that they share the same memory budget as other query buffers.

gucs.name: bioseq.index.sequence_minimizer_sort.algorithm
gucs.purpose: Change sorting algorithm used for non-grouped MPF index builds

value_descriptions.simd_u128_vqsort: Use Highway VQSort on packed 128-bit keys (implementation from C++ Highway repo).
value_descriptions.simd_u128_vec_stream_1: Use the custom SIMD sorter with one vector stream.
value_descriptions.simd_u128_vec_stream_2: Use the custom SIMD sorter with two vector streams.
value_descriptions.simd_u128_vec_stream_4: Use the custom SIMD sorter with four vector streams.

gucs.notes: SIMD versions weren't tested by me in terms of correctness and they were slower than the default

gucs.name: bioseq.index_build.run_buffer_bytes
gucs.purpose: For MPS overrides the external-sort run buffer size. Zero computes a size from the common BioseqDB memory budget.

gucs.name: bioseq.load.write_overlap.enabled
gucs.purpose: Experimental setting to use parallelized writing and decoding of data chunks through queue when loading FASTA/FASTQ files.

value_descriptions.false: Default reader perform decoding and writing (placing sequences in buffer) sequentially.
value_descriptions.true: Enable parallelized writing and decoding of data chunks through queue.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.minimizer.kmer_size
gucs.purpose: Sets the number of sequence symbols in each k-mer

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.minimizer.window_size
gucs.purpose: Sets the number of consecutive k-mers in one minimizer window

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.minimizer.algorithm
gucs.purpose: Chooses how minimizers are calculated

value_descriptions.bounded_nthash_simd: Use the bounded SIMD BioseqDB algorithm
value_descriptions.simd_minimap2_reference: Use the naive version of SIMD implementation of minimap2's
value_descriptions.two_stack_nthash: Use rolling ntHash and two-stack window-minimum inspired by simd-minimizers paper.

gucs.notes: Changing the algorithm can invalidate compatibility with saved indexes!

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.chaining.maximum_gap
gucs.purpose: Sets the requested maximum anchor gap used by chaining. Scalar (minimap2)chaining raises this limit to at least the bandwidth value.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.chaining.maximum_reference_gap
gucs.purpose: Currently unused

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.chaining.bandwidth
gucs.purpose: Despite the name it's also used by aligner stage, limits maximum distane to diagonal.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.chaining.long_join_bandwidth
gucs.purpose: Currently unused.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.chaining.maximum_skipped_anchors
gucs.purpose: Limit of consecutive updates for anchors that do not improve score (only for supported algorithms like scalar)

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.chaining.maximum_predecessors
gucs.purpose: Limits how many predecessors chainer can consider, but scalar chaining (depending on the actual algorithm) can examine one additional candidate. RMQ does not use this field.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.chaining.minimum_seed_count
gucs.purpose: Sets the minimum seed count for an accepted chain.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.chaining.minimum_score
gucs.purpose: Sets the minimum accepted chain score (the score is computed by the selected chaining algorithm)

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.chaining.gap_penalty_scale
gucs.purpose: Scales the gap penalty used by chaining (larger values penalize that contribution more strongly)

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.chaining.skip_penalty_scale
gucs.purpose: Scales the chaining skip-distance penalty.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.chaining.algorithm
gucs.purpose: Selects algorithm used for chaining

value_descriptions.simd_minimap2: BioseqDB implementation of accelerated minimap2-inspired chaining
value_descriptions.range_minimum_query: BioseqDB RMQ on AVL trees similar to what minimap2 uses

gucs.notes: Selected algorithm might still be rejected if the hardware does not support it

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.secondary.overlap_threshold
gucs.purpose: Sets the primary/secondary classification thresholds

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.secondary.uncovered_length_limit
gucs.purpose: Limits the uncovered query length used when classifying an alignment as secondary to an existing primary.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.secondary.score_ratio_threshold
gucs.purpose: Sets the secondary-to-primary score-ratio threshold. Zero bypasses this filtering step, including its secondary-count limit.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.secondary.maximum_count
gucs.purpose: Limits retained secondary alignments across the complete list passed to the filtering stage

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.scoring.match_score
gucs.purpose: Sets the score added for an aligned matching symbol.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.scoring.mismatch_penalty
gucs.purpose: Sets the score penalty for an aligned mismatch.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.scoring.short_gap_open_penalty
gucs.purpose: Sets the first gap-opening penalty. KSW2 and BlockAligner use this pair. BlockAligner requires positive opening and extension penalties whose sum is at most 128.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.scoring.short_gap_extension_penalty
gucs.purpose: Sets the first gap-extension penalty. BlockAligner requires it to be positive and its sum with the first opening penalty to be at most 128.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.scoring.long_gap_open_penalty
gucs.purpose: Sets KSW2's second gap-opening penalty. Native BlockAligner uses only the first gap-penalty pair.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.scoring.long_gap_extension_penalty
gucs.purpose: Sets KSW2's second gap-extension penalty. Native BlockAligner does not use this second pair.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.scoring.ambiguous_base_penalty
gucs.purpose: Sets the alignment penalty for ambiguous symbols on paths that support them.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.scoring.z_drop_threshold
gucs.purpose: Sets KSW2's Z-drop threshold or BlockAligner's X-drop threshold for end extensions. BlockAligner extensions require a nonnegative value.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.scoring.end_bonus
gucs.purpose: Sets KSW2's sequence-end bonus. Negative one disables the bonus. Native BlockAligner does not use it.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.seeding.maximum_occurrence
gucs.purpose: Excludes minimizer keys with more target occurrences than this limit.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.seeding.intermediate_occurrence_threshold
gucs.purpose: Currently unused

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.block_alignment.minimum_block_size
gucs.purpose: Sets BlockAligner's minimum adaptive block size. (block sizes must be powers of two and the minimum cannot exceed the maximum)

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.block_alignment.maximum_block_size
gucs.purpose: Sets BlockAligner's maximum adaptive block size. (block sizes must be powers of two and the minimum cannot exceed the maximum)

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.base_alignment.algorithm
gucs.purpose: Selects the base alignment algorithm

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.fragment_minimizer.lookup_route
gucs.purpose: Changes how grouped MPF works when reading is performed

value_descriptions.direct_compact_hash_lookup: By default read hash directly from the hash bucket.
value_descriptions.control_block_scan: Search the directory row for the hash bucket first

gucs.notes: The directory row should be faster in theory, but it's disabled, because I'm not sure if it's correct

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.grouped_soa_generation.enabled
gucs.purpose: Selects if we want to use grouped MPF version of index or non-grouped one (for writing only)

value_descriptions.true: Prefer grouped version of MPF index over non-grouped (for writing only)
value_descriptions.false: Use only non-grouped MPF when possible (for writing only)

gucs.notes: Changing this does not rewrite existing indexes, only applies to new ones and does not affect reading!

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.vulkan.enabled
gucs.purpose: Enables GPU execution

value_descriptions.true: Allow supported GPU work
value_descriptions.false: Setting aligner/chaining algorithms (or other) to Vulkan will immediately fail.

gucs.notes: GPU algorithms currently are not optimised and severly increase the query time. Enabling execution doesn't mean the GPU will be used (for example software-emulated GPUs are disabled by default). The correct GPU algorithm also need to be selected by setting respective GUCs for aligner/chaining.

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.vulkan.seed_lookup.enabled
gucs.purpose: Enabled GPU-acclelerated minimizers (reading)

value_descriptions.false: Disable GPU for reading minimizer indexes
value_descriptions.true: Enable GPU minimizer lookup (but other GPU settings apply)

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.vulkan.index_cache.enabled
gucs.purpose: Cache minimizer index data to be reused across GPU calls (applies only to single pipeline execution and transfers between GPU/CPU memory)

value_descriptions.true: Save buffer with minimizers
value_descriptions.false: GPU doesn't reuse minimizers during computation

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.vulkan.fused_frontend.enabled
gucs.purpose: Enable experimental GPU fused kernel (this doesn't work correctly)

value_descriptions.false: Leave this frontend unselected.
value_descriptions.true: Enable special optimisation for GPU kernels

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.vulkan.index_build.enabled
gucs.purpose: Enabled GPU-acclelerated minimizers (writing)

value_descriptions.false: Disable GPU for wrikting minimizer indexes
value_descriptions.true: Enable GPU minimizer index building (but other GPU settings apply)

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.vulkan.alignment_extension.enabled
gucs.purpose: Enabled CIGAR computation on GPU

value_descriptions.false: Disbable CIGAR computation on GPU
value_descriptions.true: Allow computing CIGAR on GPU (but other GPU settings apply)

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.vulkan.ordered_sketch_tile_bp
gucs.purpose: Currently unused

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.vulkan.radix_sort_digit_bits
gucs.purpose: Currently unused

gucs.name: bioseq.aligner.profiling.enabled
gucs.purpose: Enables internal profiling of the pipeline execution

value_descriptions.false: profiling measures statistics like number of minimizers/chains/timings per pipeline stage etc.
value_descriptions.true: Profiling can increase execution time

gucs.name: bioseq.scheduler.backend.max_concurrency
gucs.purpose: Limits maximum number of workers in TBB worker pool (this is separate to Postgres max workers setting)

gucs.name: bioseq.scheduler.pipeline.mode
gucs.purpose: Changes how the pipeline execution is performed

value_descriptions.task_parallel: Each query dispatches separate worker (exxtension of parallel_dispatch) and additionally each stage of pipeline can submit independent tasks to TBB worker pool
value_descriptions.single_thread: Each query dispatches separate worker, but one pipeline itself isn't parallelized.

gucs.notes: In the benchmark I use task_parallel, because it enables the highest degree of parallelism

gucs.name: bioseq.scheduler.postgres_parallel.enabled
gucs.purpose: Reduce tasks slots to 1

value_descriptions.false: Disable any parallelism completely (note that if bioseq.scheduler.pipeline.mode is set to task_parallel, then pipeline will be executed via task queues, but only one worker will be active at the time. This setting is the highest level limiter on parallelism of workers)
value_descriptions.true: Allow >1 parallel tasks limit

gucs.notes: This setting effectively forces bioseq.scheduler.backend.max_concurrency to be 1

gucs.name: bioseq.storage.sequence_shard.max_size_gib
gucs.purpose: Sets the sequence-shard size limit. If the shard table exceeds that size, then new table will be created. Setting it to 0 means that each sequence is stored in a separate table (useful for debugging, but extremally ineffective in practice)

gucs.name: bioseq_cache.query_cache.mode
gucs.purpose: Enables experimental query result cache (provided by BioseqDB bioseq_cache subextension)

value_descriptions.disabled: Do not use the query result cache (disabled due to my low confidence if it works correctly)
value_descriptions.exact_query: Reuse completed identical requests and coordinate concurrent identical computations.
value_descriptions.reusable_fragments: Permit completed-fragment reuse for providers that support it. The Bioseq alignment adapter currently supports exact reuse only (this mode is not implemented)

gucs.notes: Any mode other than 'disabled' required Postgres shared libraries reload.

gucs.name: bioseq_cache.query_cache.completed_result_ttl_ms
gucs.purpose: Maximum age of the records in the bioseq_cache tables that can be reused
